Dallas–Fort Worth tape, film, and photo transfer

Dallas–Fort Worth is large enough that “a shop in the Metroplex” can mean an hour in the car. This page covers businesses whose own sites offer tape, film, or photo transfer and that sit in, or explicitly serve, Dallas, Fort Worth, Flower Mound, Lewisville, Denton, and Richardson.

Facts checked November 19, 2026 against each business’s own website.

Call before you drive. The hours below are copied from the business site and still go stale. Ask whether they can play your exact format, what a damaged tape costs, and whether you leave with a file you can copy. If you would rather ship a mixed box, use the mail-in comparison. Shipping the only copy of a wedding tape is a real risk: photograph the labels first.

How a business gets on this page

A business is listed only when its own website states the service. The page links that source. If a price or a turnaround time is not on the site, the listing says so instead of guessing.

This is not a complete list of every studio, pharmacy, or big-box photo counter in the area. National mail-in labs are on the comparison page, not repeated under each city.

Before you go

  • Count the tapes, reels, and photos, and note the formats. VHS-C, Hi8, MiniDV, and Super 8 are not the same job as a standard VHS cassette.
  • Ask what happens if a tape is moldy, squealing, or snapped. Do not play a tape that looks moldy or that screams when it starts.
  • Ask whether you receive a file you can copy (usually MP4) or only a DVD. A DVD is a convenient extra, and a poor only copy.
  • Ask the current turnaround and whether the originals come back with the job. Get that in writing if the box is leaving your house.
  • Commercial movies and recorded television are copyrighted. A legitimate lab will refuse them.
